sonnet.problem: The right answer ("The bread won't be there") comes only from verse 26, but the card cites 16:25-26. Verse 25 is only part of the question's setup.
sonnet.rule: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

sonnet.problem: Card 9 has just established that the bread won't be there on the seventh day, so this true/false card re-asks the same fact, and the baker can answer it directly from card 9's answer.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question.

sonnet.problem: The joke "I lived in a junk drawer for years, friend, and even I would've filed a complaint" doesn't click instantly. A reader would ask what the drawer has to do with maggots, or what he would complain about. It also blurs the point of the moment, which is Moses' anger at their disobedience.
sonnet.rule: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.
